Maya (CSM): Quick sync — SentryBridge private deploy hit a blocker this morning. Network team applied egress CIDR but the app stack logs keep showing KMS 403 AccessDenied on encrypt calls. Can @Ravi or @Ana take a look? Customer is on a tight timeline and we flagged a renewal risk if we don't unblock in the next 10 days.
Ravi (Infra): On it. Do you have the exact error and the instance role ARN? Also are they using VPC endpoints for KMS or NAT-based internet egress?
Maya (CSM): Error snippet from customer: 
```
ClientError: An error occurred (AccessDeniedException) when calling the Encrypt operation: User is not authorized to perform kms:Encrypt on resource arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-efgh
```
Role: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/sentrybridge-app-Role
They're using managed NAT for internet egress; no KMS VPC endpoint configured.
Ana (Security): That 403 usually means the KMS key policy or IAM condition is blocking. I suspect the key policy has an aws:SourceVpc or aws:SourceIp condition. If traffic is SNAT'd by NAT, aws:SourceIp won't match. Quick check: can someone paste the key policy? If it uses SourceVpc, we can add the VPC ID or change to allow the role principal.
Ethan (Solutions): Alternative fast path: create a KMS VPC endpoint (PrivateLink) so traffic doesn't leave the VPC and the SourceVpc condition will match. Command: `aws ec2 create-vpc-endpoint --vpc-id vpc-012345 --service-name com.amazonaws.us-west-2.kms --vpc-endpoint-type Interface --subnet-ids subnet-aaa,subnet-bbb --security-group-ids sg-xyz` This usually resolves key policy SourceVpc checks without key policy edits.
Maya (CSM): Customer said they can't add endpoints without infra approval, and adding endpoints might need subnet capacity approvals. They asked if a temporary key policy tweak is acceptable.
Ana (Security): Temporary tweak is fine but requires audit trail and CS signoff. Suggested minimal change: add the role ARN as a principal in key policy with condition `StringEquals: {"aws:PrincipalArn": "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/sentrybridge-app-Role"}` then rotate back after endpoint is in place. I'll draft the minimal policy snippet.
Ravi (Infra): Short-term stopgap: allow egress 443 to KMS public IP ranges from the NAT to preserve the original SourceIp if the key policy checks that. Not ideal long-term. If they can whitelist the NAT egress IPs in the key policy condition `aws:SourceIp`, that also works.
Maya (CSM): Customer also reported Splunk audit-forwarder shows incomplete requestParameters for KMS operations — missing keyId, looks like the forwarder strips some fields when traffic is proxied. Any known gotchas?
Ethan (Solutions): Yes, some forwarders that sit in front of the app may rewrite or drop request metadata. Ask them to check the forwarder config (`/etc/splunk/universalforwarder/local/inputs.conf`) and enable full HTTP payload capture for the KMS agent. As a short test, can they run a single `aws kms encrypt` from a host in the VPC and forward that raw request to Splunk to compare?
Ana (Security): Also capture CloudTrail for KMS (management & data events) — CloudTrail is authoritative and will show the exact principal, source IP, and requestParameters. If CloudTrail matches the 403 source, we can map policy changes safely.
Maya (CSM): Good call. Action items: 1) Ravi to validate whether adding a KMS VPC endpoint is feasible and list subnets/security-groups (owner: Ravi). 2) Ana to prepare a minimal key policy snippet for temporary principal allow and the rollback plan (owner: Ana). 3) Ethan to provide Splunk-forwarder troubleshooting checklist (owner: Ethan). 4) Maya to schedule a 30-minute call with the customer for Tuesday 09:00 PT to review runbook and capture signoff — I'll send calendar invite.
Ravi (Infra): I'll check subnet availability and post the endpoint plan by EOD. If customer prefers not to change infra, we can also propose a dedicated NAT with static egress IP to simplify key policy conditions.
Ana (Security): Draft policy snippet (minimal): 
```
{
  "Sid": "AllowSentryBridgeRoleTemporarily",
  "Effect": "Allow",
  "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/sentrybridge-app-Role"},
  "Action": ["kms:Encrypt","kms:Decrypt"],
  "Resource": "*"
}
```
Include `Condition` if they prefer IP/VPC restrictions. Document rollout + audit log steps.
Ethan (Solutions): Splunk checklist: enable raw payload, increase sampling to 100% for this test window, and verify forwarder version >= 8.x. I'll paste a minimal `inputs.conf` snippet in the call.
